audits.mathematicalReason: Normalize the points to (i,j), where i=0,1,2,3 and j=0,1. Every nondegenerate triangle has two vertices in one row. Horizontal bases of lengths 1, 2, and 3 produce respectively 3, 3, and 2 distinct squared-side-length signatures. The eight sorted signatures are (1,1,2), (1,2,5), (1,5,10), (1,4,5), (2,2,4), (2,4,10), (1,9,10), and (2,5,9). They are mutually distinct, and SSS identifies all triangles with the same signature. This justifies canonical-representative counting under triangle congruence, rather than counting only orbits under symmetries of the entire array.

figureEvidence.fact: The eight points form two aligned rows of four equally spaced points; the row separation equals the horizontal spacing, giving three adjoining unit-square cells after normalization.

audits.mathematicalReason: Tangency of the radius-1 cookies gives center-to-center distances of 2 inches. The six outer centers form a regular hexagon around the central cookie, and their common enclosing tangent circle has the same center. Thus the dough radius is 2+1=3 inches. The scrap area is π·3²−7π·1²=2π square inches. Equal thickness preserves area when the scrap is reshaped, so πr²=2π and the physically valid radius is r=√2 inches. Circle area is the central assessed procedure; circle tangency and the principal square root are appropriate support.

figureEvidence.fact: One cookie is surrounded by a ring of six congruent cookies. Consecutive outer cookies touch, each touches the central cookie, and all six touch the enclosing dough circle.

audits.mathematicalReason: Write each pane's width as 2t and height as 5t, with t>0. The exterior width is 4(2t)+5·2=8t+10, while the exterior height is 2(5t)+3·2=10t+6. Equality of these dimensions gives t=2 and a window side length of 26 inches. Equivalently, the vertical glass total exceeds the horizontal glass total by two ratio units, while the horizontal border total exceeds the vertical border total by 4 inches; hence one ratio unit is 2 inches. Both proposed routes are valid. Equation modeling is a defensible selected method, not a universally necessary method.

figureEvidence.fact: The square window contains four columns and two rows of upright panes. Across the window there are four pane widths and five border strips; vertically there are two pane heights and three border strips.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each point block has diameter 4√2<6. Since every pair of vertices of a qualifying square is at least 6 apart, exactly one vertex must lie in each block. Let the side from the northeast vertex to the northwest vertex have displacement (−a,b), where 6≤a≤14 and |b|≤4 are integers. Quarter-turns determine the other vertices. If f(a)=5−|a−10|, the coordinate restrictions give max(f(a)−|b|,0) choices independently for each starting coordinate, hence its square placements for that displacement. Summing over a gives 85 placements for b=0 and 44, 19, 6, 1 for |b|=1,2,3,4 respectively. Thus the total is 85+2(44+19+6+1)=225. The center route independently gives 113 squares with integer centers and 112 with half-integer centers. Both routes correctly combine coordinate bounds, products within cases, and sums across cases.

figureEvidence.fact: The diagram shows four 5-by-5 lattice-point blocks, one in each quadrant, with each coordinate belonging to {−7,−6,−5,−4,−3,3,4,5,6,7}.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the bottom and top radii be R>r>0 and the sphere radius be ρ. Tangency to both bases gives frustum height 2ρ. In the axial tangential trapezoid, equal tangent lengths give slant length R+r. Pythagoras then yields (R+r)²=(R−r)²+4ρ², so ρ²=Rr. Subtracting similar cone volumes gives V_frustum=(2πρ/3)(R²+Rr+r²). Using V_sphere=4πρ³/3 and V_frustum=2V_sphere gives R²+Rr+r²=4Rr. Consequently t=R/r satisfies t²−3t+1=0. Since the bottom base is larger, t>1 selects (3+√5)/2. The supplied support nodes fit this method, but the catalog coverage of the sphere-volume step cannot be settled from the supplied definitions.

audits.mathematicalReason: The exterior cuboid has volume 12·10·5=600 cubic feet. The two opposing walls reduce the interior length and width to 10 and 8 feet. With a one-foot floor and no roof, the cavity height is 4 feet, so its volume is 10·8·4=320 cubic feet. The occupied volume is 600−320=280 cubic feet. Each block occupies one cubic foot, giving 280 blocks. Cuboid-volume subtraction also avoids double-counting wall intersections and the floor.

audits.mathematicalReason: Since AD:AB=3:2 and AB=30 inches, AD=45 inches. The rectangle area is 45·30=1350 square inches. The two semicircles together form a circle of diameter 30 inches and radius 15 inches, with area 225π square inches. Therefore the requested ratio is 1350:225π=6:π. The rectangle-area, circle-area, and ratio scopes are directly relevant, with the diameter-radius relationship appropriately supporting them.

routes.label: Separate boundary sides from shared sides

audits.mathematicalReason: The constituent polygons have 3+4+5+6+7+8=33 sides in total. There are five successive attachments, each sharing one complete edge. Each shared edge contributes twice to the constituent-side count and zero to the outer boundary, so the boundary has 33−2·5=23 sides. Equivalently, attaching an n-gon removes one old boundary edge and adds n−1, a net increase of n−2. The non-adjacent attachment sides keep consecutive joins from sharing a vertex, and consecutive polygon angles do not make straight boundary vertices. Thus the polygon-side concept and the proposed incidence-counting route are defensible.

figureEvidence.fact: The figure shows the triangle sharing a full side with the square and the pentagon attached externally to the opposite square side. These two shared segments are internal, not outer-boundary sides. The hexagon-through-octagon continuation is specified by the text rather than displayed.
